text.p: These are the leading stories in the Algerian press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- (Islamist-oriented) Movement of a Peaceful Society (MPS) and (former ruling) National Liberation Front (FLN) start behind-scenes talks to bring down Prime Minister Ahmed Ouyahia. MPS and FLN are junior partners in the government led by Ouyahia. (Some MPS deputies criticised the government programme being debated by the National Assembly (lower house). FLN was more diplomatically critical in some issues, mainly on plans to partly privatise land.)
- "Terrorist" Al Bakun Ala al Ahd (Faithful to the Oath) faction faults Armed Islamic Group (GIA). "Criminals" oppose other "criminals".
- Prime Minister Ouyahia set to reply to National Assembly members who sharply criticised his government's programme during more than 50 hours of debate.

- "Terrorist" group massacres 19 people in Ain Defla province, south of Algiers, overnight Monday-Tuesday. Four civilians were killed by having their throats slashed on Sunday when their truck was caught at a fake roadlock manned by "terrorists" in Tlemcen region, west of Algiers.
- Main workers' union is preparing a march to protest at violence. The protest may take place on August 20, coinciding with Martyrs' Day.
- The government will sponsor a conference grouping experts and farmers' representatives to deal with land ownership.
- The National Assembly is expected to endorse the government programme without change in its main planks.
